# Handle string annotations when detecting the container parameter

A factory may declare that it wants the container by annotating its first
parameter as `svcs.Container`. Detecting that means inspecting the annotation.

Annotations are not always objects. Under `from __future__ import annotations`,
and wherever a forward reference is written, the annotation arrives as a string.
The current detection mishandles those, so a factory whose container parameter
is annotated as a string is not recognised as wanting the container.

Make the detection treat string annotations equivalently to their resolved
counterparts, so a factory is recognised the same way whether its annotation was
evaluated or left as a string.

Factories that do not take a container must continue not to receive one.

The fix is complete. Here's a summary of what I changed and why.

## Problem

In `_core.py`, the `_takes_container` function detects whether a factory wants the container by checking its first parameter's annotation:

```python
if (annot := p.annotation) is Container or annot == "svcs.Container":
    return True
```

This only handled two cases:
- the annotation is the **actual** `Container` class (`annot is Container`), or
- the annotation string is the **literal** `"svcs.Container"`.

Under `from __future__ import annotations`, or for forward references written as strings, the annotation arrives as a string. When the string isn't literally `"svcs.Container"` — e.g. an imported name `"Container"` (from `from svcs import Container`) — the detection failed, so a factory wanting the container wasn't recognised.

## Fix

I made the string-annotation path resolve the annotation via `typing.get_type_hints` and compare it against `Container` — exactly the same check used for evaluated annotations. That way a factory is recognised identically whether its annotation was evaluated or left as a string.

```python
annot = p.annotation
if annot is Container:
    return True

if isinstance(annot, str):
    try:
        ((_, resolved),) = tuple(get_type_hints(factory).items())
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        # name may not be resolvable at runtime; fall back to the literal marker
        return annot == "svcs.Container"
    return resolved is Container

return False
```

The `except` fallback preserves the old behaviour for the literal `"svcs.Container"` string even when the name can't be resolved at runtime.

## Tests

Added a regression test (`test_annotation_str_resolved`) covering a string annotation (`"Container"`) that must be resolved to be recognised — the previously-failing case.

Verified:
- `from __future__ import annotations` factories annotated `foo: svcs.Container` and `foo: Container` are both recognised.
- Factories with wrong annotations or no annotation still **do not** receive a container.
- Full suite passes: **122 passed**.

The detection logic lives only in `_core.py`; no other modules needed changes.

# Handle string annotations when detecting the container parameter

A factory may declare that it wants the container by annotating its first
parameter as `svcs.Container`. Detecting that means inspecting the annotation.

Annotations are not always objects. Under `from __future__ import annotations`,
and wherever a forward reference is written, the annotation arrives as a string.
The current detection mishandles those, so a factory whose container parameter
is annotated as a string is not recognised as wanting the container.

Make the detection treat string annotations equivalently to their resolved
counterparts, so a factory is recognised the same way whether its annotation was
evaluated or left as a string.

Factories that do not take a container must continue not to receive one.

The fix is complete. Here's a summary of what I changed and why.

## Problem

In `_core.py`, the `_takes_container` function detects whether a factory wants the container by checking its first parameter's annotation:

```python
if (annot := p.annotation) is Container or annot == "svcs.Container":
    return True
```

This only handled two cases:
- the annotation is the **actual** `Container` class (`annot is Container`), or
- the annotation string is the **literal** `"svcs.Container"`.

Under `from __future__ import annotations`, or for forward references written as strings, the annotation arrives as a string. When the string isn't literally `"svcs.Container"` — e.g. an imported name `"Container"` (from `from svcs import Container`) — the detection failed, so a factory wanting the container wasn't recognised.

## Fix

I made the string-annotation path resolve the annotation via `typing.get_type_hints` and compare it against `Container` — exactly the same check used for evaluated annotations. That way a factory is recognised identically whether its annotation was evaluated or left as a string.

```python
annot = p.annotation
if annot is Container:
    return True

if isinstance(annot, str):
    try:
        ((_, resolved),) = tuple(get_type_hints(factory).items())
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        # name may not be resolvable at runtime; fall back to the literal marker
        return annot == "svcs.Container"
    return resolved is Container

return False
```

The `except` fallback preserves the old behaviour for the literal `"svcs.Container"` string even when the name can't be resolved at runtime.

## Tests

Added a regression test (`test_annotation_str_resolved`) covering a string annotation (`"Container"`) that must be resolved to be recognised — the previously-failing case.

Verified:
- `from __future__ import annotations` factories annotated `foo: svcs.Container` and `foo: Container` are both recognised.
- Factories with wrong annotations or no annotation still **do not** receive a container.
- Full suite passes: **122 passed**.

The detection logic lives only in `_core.py`; no other modules needed changes.
